Subject: Eval scope & MAP — timeline request

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the throughput profile you showed. We want to formalize an evaluation MAP so internal stakeholders can sign off. High level ask: a 4–6 week evaluation that proves production latency under 99th percentile, token-cost comparisons for the primary workflow, and a small integration test to validate our data handling (no PHI in the sample set).

Could you share a MAP that includes:
- Success criteria and exit gates (what constitutes pass/fail)
- Concrete acceptance tests (how we measure)
- Proposed milestones and cutover timeline for a pilot->production step

Procurement is looping in parallel for SOW/pricing; we need to align on dates so they can calendar resources.

Thanks — Ellen
Director, Platform Engineering
ClearWell Therapeutics

Ellen — thanks, this is helpful. I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an SOW draft for procurement. Below is a concise summary so teams can align quickly.

Attachment: "sofia_MAP_v1.pdf"; "SOW_draft_ClearWell.docx"

Summary (pass/fail-focused):
- Primary success criteria:
  - 99th percentile latency <= 450ms for the primary generate route (payloads matching your sample distribution).
  - Production token cost per 1k tokens within 12% of the estimate in the SOW.
  - Integration smoke test: end-to-end inference with your anonymized sample set (1000 requests) with zero data leakage incidents and correct redaction behavior.

- Exit gates (fail conditions that stop the evaluation):
  - Sustained 99th percentile latency > 700ms for > 30 minutes under expected load profile.
  - Token cost estimate variance > 25% after batching/quantization.
  - Any confirmed data handling issue during the integration test.

- Acceptance tests / how we'll measure:
  1) Latency SLO test: 10k-request synthetic run replaying your traffic distribution (we'll supply a runner).
  2) Cost verification: identical workloads run across baseline and tuned configs to produce token-cost delta report.
  3) Functional smoke: 1000 anonymized live requests validated for redaction/no-exfiltration.
  4) Stability run: 24-hour continuous run at expected concurrency with health checks and KV-cache hit rate > 70%.

- Proposed milestones (6-week plan):
  Week 0: Kickoff, account access, and sample set handoff
  Week 1: Baseline runs + initial tuning suggestions (batching, quant profiles)
  Week 2–3: Integration tests, latency SLO tuning, and mid-eval checkpoint
  Week 4: Cost verification runs and evidence capture
  Week 5: Stakeholder review + run remediation for any failing acceptance tests
  Week 6: Go/no-go decision and optional pilot cutover plan

Next steps: If that looks good, we suggest a kickoff on Monday 16 Feb so Procurement can finish the SOW review the week of the 16th. Karthik / Lauren / Marissa — please review acceptance-test definitions below and flag any missing operational proofs.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sofia — good first pass. A few technical clarifications and additions to the acceptance tests that will matter in production:

- Latency test: define the payload-size buckets (small/median/large) and include both cold-start and warmed KV-cache runs. We should require meets-SLO for warmed runs and document cold-start recovery curves.
- Cost verification: include a test for the configured KV cache hit-rate impact on token count (we should capture tokens saved by prefix cache).
- Safety regressions: run the sample set through our output-safety filter and record any false positives/negatives vs. your baseline.
- Deterministic pass criteria for stability: define max allowed error rate (5xx responses + bad outputs) <= 0.2% during the 24-hour run.

Suggested changes to exit gates (additions):
- Major regression in hallucination rate vs. baseline (>15% worse on target metric)
- Any endpoint-auth failure during integration test window

I'll add these to the MAP and upload v1.1. Also: we'll provide a small test harness repo for ClearWell to run the acceptance tests locally if you prefer.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — a couple procurement/contract items to call out so acceptance is actionable from a legal/finance perspective: 

- SOW needs a clear definition for "accepted evidence" (we recommend: run logs, perf artifacts, cost delta spreadsheet, and a signed Acceptance Memo from ClearWell engineering).
- Proposed payment milestones: 50% on evaluation start, 25% on mid-eval checkpoint (Week 3), 25% on acceptance memo sign-off. Procurement asked for line-item pricing for pilot scale (tokens/month tiers).
- Data handling: add explicit clause for sample data (ownership = ClearWell, Redwood will not store beyond test window; auto-delete 7 days after run unless otherwise agreed).

I'll attach a short SOW redline and a one-page "Acceptance Memo" template. If ClearWell agrees, procurement can pre-approve and speed the PO once dates are locked.
